lang.name: English
site.name: AI Academy
site.tagline: A personal learning space for a software engineer.
site.description: Daily AI engineering lessons with exercises, from tokens to agents. Readable on desktop and phone, online or offline.
site.footer: Personal AI engineering course. Your notes and progress stay on this device unless you sign in to sync them.
home.intro: Short daily lessons with runnable exercises. Predict, run, compare, and keep your notes and progress in sync across devices.
home.continue.start.hint: No progress yet. Pick a course below, or start with the first lesson of AI Engineering.
home.continue.allDone: You have completed every published lesson. New lessons appear here as they are added.
home.review.hint: Questions you marked for review and lessons you bookmarked.
home.search.label: Search lessons and notes
home.search.none: Nothing matches. Try a shorter word.
home.planned.hint: Planned lessons are not written yet. They show the direction of the track.
home.track.empty: No lessons published yet in this track.
home.notes.hint: Short references that sit beside the lessons.
home.data.hint: Everything you type is saved on this device immediately. Sign in to keep it in sync across your devices.
lesson.label: Lesson {n}
lesson.regenerated: Regenerated lesson. The original text was not available, so this page was rebuilt from the course summary and progress tracker. It will be replaced if the original is recovered.
lesson.untranslated: This lesson has not been translated yet. You are reading the English version.
lesson.exercise.run: Run it from the project folder:
lesson.notes.hint: Write your predictions before you run the exercise, then your observations after. Saved as you type.
lesson.notes.placeholder: What do I expect to see, and why?
lesson.notes.nostorage: Browser storage is unavailable, so this text will not be kept.
lesson.quiz.hint: Answer in your head first, then reveal. Mark what you want to see again.
note.label: Concept note
offline.cached: Offline. This page is available from the local copy.
account.title: Settings and sync
account.notConfigured: Cloud sync is not configured on this site yet. Your progress and notes are saved on this device. See docs/SETUP_AND_DEPLOYMENT.md in the repository to enable it.
account.intro: Sign in with your email to keep progress, notes, bookmarks and preferences in sync across devices. No password: you receive a one-time link.
account.sent: Check your inbox. Open the link on this device to finish signing in.
account.signOut.hint: Signing out keeps a local copy on this device.
account.deleteCloud.confirm: Delete all your synced learning data from the cloud? This device keeps its local copy until you clear it.
account.imported: Imported {n} items. Newer entries won; notes that differed were merged.
account.importFailed: That file is not an AI Academy export.
account.clearLocal.confirm: Remove all progress, notes and preferences from this device?
account.loadFailed: The sync service could not be loaded. You can keep working; data stays on this device.
merge.title: Merge your progress?
merge.body: This device has learning data and your account already has data from elsewhere. Choose what to do. Nothing is deleted automatically.
merge.merge.hint: Keeps completed lessons from both, uses the newest version of each entry, and keeps both versions of notes that differ.
merge.cloud.hint: Replaces this device's data with what is in your account.
pwa.install: Add this site to your home screen for an app-like, offline experience.
home.courses.hint: Each course is a sequence of short lessons with exercises.
course.label: Course
settings.appearance.hint: System follows your device's light or dark setting.
runner.unsupported: This browser can't run Python here. Use the commands under “Run on your computer”.
runner.missing: {name} isn't available in this build of the site yet. Use the reference output or run it on your computer.
runner.hint: Runs in your browser on this device. The first run downloads about {size}; after that it starts in a second or two, also offline. Edits are saved and synced with your notes.
runner.predictFirst: Write your predictions in My notes before you run.
runner.reference.hint: Recorded by running the original script with real Python and the real packages on {date}.
lab.label: Lab
home.labs.hint: Interactive experiments that run real models in your browser.
lab.download: Runs entirely in your browser. The first use downloads about {size}; after that it starts quickly, also offline.
lab.inspector.similarity: Cosine similarity of the two sentence embeddings
lab.inspector.simNote: Mean-pooled {dims}-dimension embeddings, normalized, as in lesson 2.
lab.inspector.attentionHint: Rows are the token doing the looking (query), columns the token it looks at (key). Each row sums to 1. Pick a layer, then a head; the first cell shows the average of all twelve heads.
lab.inspector.head: Head {h}
lab.inspector.heatLabel: Attention heatmap, {title}. Use the table for exact values.
lab.inspector.scale: Color shows attention weight on a square-root scale.
lab.inspector.normsHint: Average length of the token vectors after the embeddings and after each block. Compare with lesson 4.
lab.inspector.normsLabel: Line chart of the mean residual-stream norm per layer
lab.train.corpus: Training text (edit it, or paste your own)
lab.train.summary: {words} words, {v} distinct tokens. A model that knows nothing scores ln(V) = {uniform}; this run ended at {final}. The best a bigram model can do on this text is {floor}.
lab.train.lossLabel: Line chart of training loss per step. Final loss {final}, best possible {floor}.
lab.train.ckTitle: Inside the model, step by step
lab.train.ckHint: Pick a checkpoint and a word to see what the model predicts next at that point in training. Temperature reshapes the distribution; top-p removes the tail (marked ✕).
lab.train.distNote: Entropy {entropy} nats. Bars marked ✕ are outside the top-p nucleus and are never sampled.
pred.title: Your predictions
pred.hint: Commit to an answer and a confidence before you run anything. The site checks you against the real output and tracks your calibration over time.
pred.wrong: Not quite. The real value is {answer}.
pred.missing: Answer every question and pick a confidence first.
pred.locked: Locked in. Now run the exercise, then check.
home.intuition.hint: How often your locked-in predictions were right, grouped by how confident you said you were. A well-calibrated learner is right about 90% of the time when they say 90%.
home.intuition.empty: No checked predictions yet. Lessons have a Your predictions card in the hands-on challenge.
home.intuition.chart: Calibration: stated confidence against how often you were right
prov.title: How this lesson was made and checked
prov.claims: {n} numbers in the text verified against the exercise output
prov.claimsPending: {n} numbers in the text, verified on the next CI build
prov.runsReal: Exercise runs in your browser and matches real Python exactly
prov.identical: Exercise runs in your browser with output identical to real Python and real packages
prov.close: Exercise runs in your browser; numbers within {d} of real Python and PyTorch
prov.notRun: Exercise not yet checked in CI
prov.hint: Every check runs on each deploy. A lesson whose numbers drift from its exercise fails the build instead of shipping.
runner.shared: You opened a shared version of this exercise. It is not saved yet.
